translationRepairs: Renjun answered: "Zu Chongzhi of Liu-Song founded precession; Zhang Zexuan of Sui and others refined it.
Renjun answered: "Zu Chongzhi of Liu-Song founded precession; Zhang Zhouxuan of Sui and others refined it.
張胄玄: 胄 is read zhòu, so the name romanizes as Zhang Zhouxuan, not Zexuan.
Master Kong's commentary: 'Gathered means in conjunction.
The Chinese says only 孔氏 (Master Kong / the Kong commentary); the translation adds an unsupported identification as Kong Yingda (the literal field reads "Kong's commentary").
In year nine, Cui Shanyi and Xiaotong revised dozens of rules.
In year nine, Cui Shanwei, Chief Minister of Justice, and Xiaotong were ordered to recheck the calendar; Shanwei changed several dozen items.
崔善為: 為 is read wéi, so the name is Cui Shanwei, not Shanyi; also restores the omitted office 大理卿 and the edict.
The sun's motion through lodges shifts like a gnomon shadow; lodge drift moves the ecliptic too.
The sun's passage through the lodge degrees is like a courier passing relay stations; once the lodge degrees drift, the ecliptic shifts with them.
郵傳之過 means the passing of a postal relay (courier stations), not a gnomon shadow; the translation substitutes an unrelated image.
Early Zhenguan, Li Chunfeng petitioned on eighteen points; seven revisions followed his method after Shanyi compared both schools.

Early in Zhenguan, Li Chunfeng, attendant in the Grand Astrologer's office, again petitioned on eighteen points; an edict again ordered Shanwei to assess the two schools, and seven items were changed to follow Chunfeng.
善為 is Cui Shanwei (為 read wéi), not Shanyi; also restores Chunfeng's post 直太史 and the edict to Shanwei.
In a gengzi year the court reverted to Renjun's mean new moon through Lindé year one.
On a gengzi day an edict restored Renjun's mean new moon, which remained in use until Lindé year one.
庚子 here stands alone as a sexagenary day marker following the year-nineteen context, not a year; the edict (詔) is also restored.
